Below is the statement, formatted as a formal document that can go into your file and be copied to Mrs. Okafor. I left your name and signature blank — fill those in before you turn it in.

---

**WRITTEN STATEMENT**

**Bus 41 — Route 9 (Fairmont Elementary)**
Dayton, Ohio

**Date:** November 3, 2020

**To:** Mrs. Okafor, Parent/Guardian of Amara Okafor, Kindergarten, Fairmont Elementary

**From:** [Your Name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9

**Re:** Incident of Tuesday, October 27 — Stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am writing this statement at the request of my supervisor, Mrs. Darlene [Last Name], in response to the complaint you filed with the transportation office concerning the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27. Because this document is being placed in my personnel file and a copy is being sent to you, I want to set out the facts as clearly and respectfully as I can. I have nothing but good feelings for you and for Amara, and I have been glad to drive Amara on my route every day. My hope is that this statement helps put the record straight and moves us past this.

**Purpose**

I want you to know at the outset that I am not writing this statement in order to dispute your account of how this felt from your end of the street. A kindergartener is not supposed to be frightened, and I understand that you were frightened. I have grandchildren of my own, and I would have been frightened too. What I do want on paper is the simple fact that I followed the procedure the district has written for me, and that procedure is what the record should reflect.

**The Stop and What I Observed**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was driving the afternoon run on Bus 41, Route 9, serving Fairmont Elementary. My last stop of the afternoon was the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, where Amara is picked up.

My schedule shows a 3:50 p.m. arrival at that stop. I arrived at 3:52 p.m. I did not pull away immediately. I waited at the corner until approximately 3:55 p.m., which gave me a little more than the scheduled time and roughly a full minute more than my usual practice, in case anyone was walking up or running late.

During that time, I did not see an adult at the stop. I want to be as specific as I can here, because I know this is the point on which our accounts differ. You have told the office that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved to me. I did not see you wave. On the side of the street where you were parked, there was a box truck positioned near the corner, and from the driver's seat of the bus that truck blocked my sight line across Brandt Street entirely. I was looking straight at that corner and I could not see a person standing at it. I want to be clear that this is not an accusation against you. I believe you were there. I simply could not see you, and it is entirely possible that you were waving at a spot where the truck was between us.

**The Rule for Kindergarten Riders**

Amara's bag carries the green tag. In our district, the green tag designates a kindergarten student who requires a responsible adult to be physically present at the stop before the student may be released from the bus. The district procedure for a kindergartener with a green tag is not discretionary on my part. If no adult is present at the stop, the student stays on the bus, the bus returns to the school, and the transportation office is contacted so that the parent can be notified and the child can be released into the school's care.

Because no adult was visible at the corner, I was required to keep Amara on the bus and return her to Fairmont. That is what I did.

**What I Did to Reach Someone**

At 3:56 p.m., with Amara still on the bus and no adult at the stop, I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school, Fairmont Elementary, and it was my understanding that the office was to reach out to the parent that the child was being returned to the school and could be picked up there. I was also carrying three more stops and fourteen students still on board at that time, so I proceeded with my route as required.

**Return to School**

I arrived back at Fairmont Elementary at 4:31 p.m. I did not leave Amara in the office alone. I walked her in myself and handed her directly to Mrs. Petrakis in the office. She was not scared or upset. She was coloring on her folder and, when she asked whether she could ride on some more of the route, I told her that we were going on a little extra trip and that she would see her mom soon. I point this out only because I believe it reflects how Amara herself experienced the afternoon, and I would like that to be part of the record as well.

**Regarding the Statement That I Drove Off Laughing**

You told the office that I drove away from the stop laughing. I did not laugh. What I was doing as we pulled out was telling a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down, because she had stood up in her seat to look out the window. I want to make sure the record is accurate on this point, and I am sorry that it looked otherwise from where you were parked.

**A Note About My Own Record**

I have driven for this district for twenty-eight years and I have never received a write-up. I include that fact not as a defense, but because it is accurate, and because I would rather you hear it from me directly than infer it. I have also had an experience similar to this one on my route, some years back, with a different family on my run. In that instance, when there was no adult at a stop, I kept the child on the bus and returned the child to the school, and the family later contacted the office to thank me. I mention it because it shows that what happened with Amara is the system working as it was designed to work, and that it did not mean anyone was in trouble or being abandoned at the curb.

**My Request That the Bus Camera Footage Be Pulled**

I am respectfully asking the transportation office to pull and preserve the camera footage from Bus 41 for the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27, 2020, covering the period from approximately 3:45 p.m. through 4:35 p.m. The camera will show my arrival at the Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street stop, the length of time I waited, the position of the box truck on the street, the fact that I did not leave the corner until approximately 3:55 p.m., and my return to Fairmont. If the corner business, the laundromat, or the property on that side of Brandt Street has exterior camera coverage, I would ask that it be preserved as well, since it may be able to show where you were standing.

I would ask that this footage be preserved promptly, as bus camera recordings are retained on a short cycle and are overwritten.

**A Point About Safety**

I would like to explain why I did not get out of the bus and walk across to the laundromat to look for you. I had fourteen children on the bus. A driver who leaves a loaded bus with fourteen students unattended, on any street, in any weather, in order to search for one adult, is putting every one of those children at risk and putting themselves in a position where they could be held responsible for whatever happens to that bus. That is not a decision I can make, and it is not a decision the district's procedures allow me to make. I do not say that to minimize your concern. I say it so that you understand the reasoning was not indifference to you and Amara.

**What I Am Asking Going Forward**

I am asking for one specific adjustment, and I do not believe it is an unreasonable one: that at the Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street stop, you stand on the bus side of the street, or step out of your car and stand where you can be seen from the driver's seat. If the bus is early or late by a minute or two, a driver who can see you waiting at the corner has no reason to keep a child on the bus, and I will not have any difficulty releasing Amara to you. That is a small change on your part and it removes all doubt for everyone involved, including the next driver on this route.

**Closing**

I am glad to keep driving Amara. I have had her on my run and I enjoy having her aboard. Nothing in this situation changes my willingness to do that, and I would like to see this resolved in a way that lets everyone continue working comfortably together.

I did what the district's procedure requires in this situation, and I am asking that this statement be entered into the record to show that. I am not sorry for following the rule that is there to protect children like Amara. I am genuinely sorry that your daughter had a bad afternoon, and I am sorry that you were left worrying. If you would like to talk about this by phone rather than on paper, I am happy to do that at whatever time is convenient for you.

Please feel free to contact me or the transportation office with any questions.

Respectfully submitted,

_______________________________
[Your Name]
Driver, Bus 41 — Route 9
Fairmont Elementary
Dayton, Ohio
Telephone: [number]

**cc:** Transportation Office — personnel file
Darlene [Last Name], Supervisor, Transportation

---

**Two small notes before you submit:**

Check your district's actual terminology with the office — I wrote "green tag," "Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street," and the return-to-school procedure as you described them, but if your policy uses different wording (for example, "escort required" or a specific policy number), match it exactly, since your statement and the policy are stronger when they use the same words.

Also, if you want it to read a little more like your own voice, the paragraph in brackets is the one to adjust, and I can re-do it either warmer or more formal depending on how you want it to land with her.
